name: Malpua (Jharkhand Style)
instructions: 1. In a large bowl, whisk together mashed bananas, jaggery/sugar, and milk until smooth.
2. Gradually add wheat flour, fennel seeds, cardamom powder, and salt, mixing to form a thick, lump-free batter.
3. Cover and let the batter rest for at least 30 minutes to ensure the right texture.
4. Heat ghee in a shallow pan on medium heat.
5. Pour a ladleful of batter into the hot ghee, letting it spread into a small circular shape.
6. Fry on both sides until deep golden brown and crispy.
7. Remove and drain excess ghee before serving warm.
description: Malpua is a beloved traditional dessert in Jharkhand, often prepared during festivals like Holi, Diwali, and weddings. Unlike the syrup-soaked versions found in other parts of India, the Jharkhandi style is characterized by the use of mashed bananas in the batter, which gives it a unique moist texture and distinct flavor, often enjoyed alongside savory vegetable curries.
